text: Hi, I'm Volta. Welcome to the Voltex lab. Let's build a real circuit board together, and if something burns, that's how we learn.
Free build mode. Drag any part onto the board, route your traces, then flip the power on.
Mission one. Connect the battery, resistor and LED. The resistor starts at ten ohms. Power it on and watch closely.
Your LED is glowing at a safe twenty milliamps. That is Ohm's law doing its job.
Mission two. Put a switch in series, so it can break the loop and turn the LED on and off.
Click, on. Click, off. Every power switch in the world works exactly like that.
Mission three. Two equal resistors split nine volts in half. Route them, then measure the middle with the probe.
Four and a half volts. You just built a voltage divider, the way chips read sensors.
Mission four. A tiny base current lets the transistor switch a much bigger one. Route it, then hold the button.
Small current in, big current out. That is how microcontrollers drive motors and lights.
Mission five. Build a night light. When the room gets dark, the light sensor should switch the LED on.
Lights out, LED on. Street lights use exactly this trick.
Mission six. Some wires must cross. Copper on one layer can't, so drop one to the bottom layer with a via.
Two layers, zero shorts. You're routing like a real board designer now.
Mission seven, the famous five five five timer. Route it right and the LED will blink about once a second.
Blink, blink. The capacitor charges and empties, and the five five five keeps the rhythm.
Final mission. Design anything you like, clear every design rule check, and send it to the factory.
Clean design, sent to fab. That board could be made for real. I'm proud of you.
New project from the library. Follow the dashed lines, route every connection, then power it up.
It works! Now try changing a value and see what happens. That's how engineers learn.
Short circuit! The battery's plus and minus are touching. Find the wire that connects them directly and remove it.
Careful, this LED has no resistor. Without one, it takes all the current it can get and burns out.
Too much current here. Try a bigger resistor. Supply minus LED voltage, divided by twenty milliamps.
Pop. That LED just burnt out. Fix the resistor value, then click replace part in the inspector.
Something overheated and burnt out. Check what's limiting the current, then replace the part.
That capacitor is in backwards. Electrolytics have polarity. The stripe goes to minus.
This part is the wrong way round. Rotate it twice with the R key to flip it.
The LED is backwards. Current flows from the anode, A, to the cathode, K. Flip it with R, R.
There's a pin with nothing connected. Follow the dashed line and route it.
That trace is too thin for the current it carries. Pick a wider trace, so it doesn't heat up.
These two wires are too close. Keep at least point two millimetres between different nets, or the factory can't make it.
Two parts are sitting on top of each other. Drag one of them to some free space.
That part is hanging off the edge of the board. Move it inside the outline.
Sharp corner alert. Corners tighter than ninety degrees trap acid in the factory. Use forty five degree bends.
The five five five is stuck off. Pin four is reset. Connect it to V C C, and it wakes up.
There's no battery on the board yet. Every circuit needs a power source.
Power on. Watch the current flow along your traces.
Nice, your first trace. Copper traces are the wires of a circuit board.
That's a via, a tiny plated hole connecting the top and bottom layers.
The probe measures voltage from the battery's minus side. Click any copper to read it.
Design rule check passed. No errors, no warnings. Lovely clean board.
Not yet. The factory won't accept a board with design rule errors. Fix the list first.
This is fab view. Green solder mask, gold pads, white silkscreen, just like it comes from the factory.
You're doing great. Every engineer burns a few LEDs along the way.
There's no clean path on this layer, so that trace touches other copper. Press L to switch layers, or drop a via with V.
Oh, you're back. Let's keep building.
